info.description: Filinq register v8.46.0: `publicationRecord` 1.1.1 stores the Woo category as OpenCatalogi's code (infocat009); an old TOOI code is translated at hand-off. Before that, v8.44.0: inbound classification. New schema `classificationResult` 1.0.0 (a suggested document type, correspondent and dossier for one inbound file and what a person decided about it; corrections kept beside the suggestion); `intakeDocument` 1.3.0 gains `documentType` and `correspondent`, set only by a confirmed classification. Before that, v8.43.0: guided document wizard. New schema `wizardDefinition` 1.0.0 (ordered questions with skip logic in front of one template); `generatedDocument` 1.6.0 gains `wizardContext` (the wizard, its version and the answers of the run that generated the document). Before that, v8.42.0: email ingestion. New schema `emailDocument` 1.0.0 (one row per email filed from a watched inbox folder into a dossier: the .eml, its PDF/A copy, the envelope, the thread headers and a sha256 of the file; a file that could not be filed is a failed row with its reason). Before that, v8.41.0: document sanitization. New schema `sanitizationRecord` 1.0.0 (one row per sanitization run: the source file, the clean file beside it, the trigger, and how many items were removed per category; counts only, never the removed content). Before that, v8.40.0: contract pages. `documentContract` 1.1.0 is searchable now that its detail page exists. Before that, v8.39.0: contracts. New schema `documentContract` 1.0.0 (parties, key dates, value, documents and signature of a contract; a declared lifecycle draft, active, renewed, terminated, expired; scheduled reminders for the notice deadline and the end date). Before that, v8.38.0: `signingRequest` 1.10.0 declares every status move the signing service makes (decline from pending, cancel and expire while under way). Before that, v8.37.0: signing envelopes. New schema `signingEnvelope` 1.0.0 (several documents signed in one ceremony: the member requests, the initiator, the signers, a status rolled up from the members). `signingRequest` 1.9.0 and `signerRecord` 1.6.0 gain `envelopeRef`; a signer record in an envelope gets the envelope's one notification instead of one per document. Before that, v8.36.0: signing field placement. `signingRequest` 1.8.0 gains `fieldPlacements` (per signer: page, a box in page-relative coordinates, one of five field types). Before that, v8.30.0: entity-search. New schema `entitySearchLog` 1.0.0 (one append-only row per entity search or entity detail view: who, when, the sha256 digest of the query, never the query itself). Before that, v8.29.0: erase-a-person-while-the-records-stay. v8.28.0: e-discovery-legal-hold. New schema `legalHoldCase` 1.0.0 (a legal matter and the records it freezes: scope, custodian, reason, placement per record, active to released). Before that, v8.27.0: reversible-pseudonymization. New schema `pseudonymMap` 1.0.0 (the key that turns the placeholders in one reversibly anonymised copy back into names: encrypted with the server secret before it is written, `writeOnly` so no read returns it, one per anonymisation link). `anonymizationLink` moves to 1.2.0 with `mappingRef`, the map a reversible run kept; empty for an irreversible run. Before that, v8.26.0: intake-ocr-on-arrival. `intakeDocument` 1.2.0 gains `contentText` (the text OCR read from the file on arrival). Before that, v8.25.0: ocr-trigger-surface. New schema `ocrResult` 1.0.0 (what the last text recognition run on a file found: confidence, languages, DPI, text length, when, who started it and the engine version; never the text). Before that, v8.24.0: woo-publicatie-pipeline. New schemas `publicationRecord` 1.0.0 (a document on its way to the publication platform: the readiness checks, the Woo metadata, the platform's publication id, withdrawal and destruction date) and `publicationLogEntry` 1.0.0 (an append-only step log). PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.23.0: libresign-signing-provider. `signingRequest` moves to 1.7.0 with `externalId`, the request at the signing provider that runs the signer flow (for LibreSign its file uuid). Optional, so existing rows stay valid. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.22.0: print-jobs-in-the-app. New schema `printJob` 1.0.0: a job of letters sent to print, its status from rendering to printed or failed, and the PDFs as files in the app data folder. Job state used to live in app configuration with the whole PDF base64-encoded; a repair step moves those entries here. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.21.0: periodic-documents-on-a-schedule. `periodicDocument` moves to 1.1.0 with `lastRunError` and `lastRunErrorAt`: an hourly job runs every active schedule whose cadence has come round, and a run that fails writes why on the schedule instead of in a log nobody reads, while `lastRunDocument` keeps pointing at the last good document. Both are optional, so existing rows stay valid. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.20.0: portal-signing-surface. `signerRecord` moves to 1.5.0 with `signatureAssurance` (SES or AES), the assurance a portal signature records: never above the portal session trust and never QES. Optional, so existing rows stay valid. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.17.1: template-slug-inside-properties. v8.16.1 wrote the template's new `slug` and `tenantId` definitions beside the schema's own keys instead of inside `properties`. The `slug` definition was a duplicate JSON key, so the schema's slug `template` was replaced by a property definition object, and OpenRegister refuses a schema fragment without a string slug: the whole `template` schema was skipped while the import reported success. Both definitions now sit inside `properties`, and `template` moves to 1.4.1 so the corrected schema reaches every install. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.17.0: signer-identity-rails, guardian consent (learniq round 1 decision D11). `signerRecord` moves to 1.3.0 with `role`, `guardianForSignerId`, `guardianAct`, `consentStatement`, `guardianRef`, a hidden `birthDate` and `actingIdentity`; `signingRequest` moves to 1.5.0 with `guardianConsentAge` and `consentBasis`. A signer under the age of consent (admin setting `signing_guardian_consent_age`, default 16) signs only with a guardian on the same request, and the completed request records both signers and the basis, never the birth date. Every addition is optional, so existing rows stay valid. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.16.1: filinq-configurable-report-templates. `template` moves 1.3.0 to 1.4.0 and gains `slug` and `tenantId`, so another app (learniq report cards) can ask for a template by a stable slug, scoped per school with a namespace-wide fallback, without knowing its UUID. The patch bump exists so the schema change reaches installs that already imported v8.16.0. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.16.0: leaf-integrations. Six schemas opt into the standard OpenRegister leaves through `configuration.linkedTypes`: `signingRequest` (mail, calendar), `signerRecord` (contacts), `publicationConsent` (mail, calendar, deck), `correspondence` (mail), `generatedDocument` (files) and `dossier` (files, deck). `publicationConsent` and `correspondence` also carry a `mailObjectTemplate`, so an objection mail or an inbound case mail can seed a record from the NC Mail sidebar, in its initial state and nothing further. Every template key was cross-checked against that schema’s own `properties` map, because an unknown key fails the whole register import. No property, `required` list or authorization block changes, and the agent-facing MCP surface is untouched. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.15.0: redaction-and-what-leaves-the-building, the verdict. `anonymizationLink` moves to 1.1.0 and carries the irreversibility verifier's answer about the bytes that were actually written: `verificationVerdict` (clean, leaking or unverifiable), `verificationOutputMode`, `verificationRoutes`, `verificationLeakRoutes` and `verifiedAt`. The verdict is recorded even when it is `unverifiable`, because an empty field and a clean verdict look the same to anything filtering on "was this copy checked" and one of them means nobody looked. The output mode is stored beside the verdict because a PDF/UA rewrite can put a text layer back: the answer holds for the mode that produced this copy and for no other. THE BUMP IS THE POINT AND IT IS NOT COSMETIC HERE: this schema is `hardValidation: true`, so on an install that has not re-imported, the five new fields are undeclared and OpenRegister REFUSES the whole link write, which loses the source-to-copy pairing rather than only the verdict. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.14.0: intake-failure-reaches-someone. `intakeDocument` gains `readingState`, `readingError` and `readingUpdatedAt`, and an `x-openregister-notifications` rule that tells the registrars when documents could not be read. The rule coalesces on an hour window and digests at 08:30, so a scanner jamming at 02:00 produces one message rather than one per page. It is addressed to docudesk-woo-officers, which ships EMPTY like every declared group: openregister now refuses a recipient that can never resolve at declaration time and records a rule that reached nobody at dispatch, once per run, so an unstaffed group is visible rather than silent. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.13.0: erase-a-person-while-the-records-stay. Adds `subjectErasureRequest`, a betrokkene asking to come out of the documents while the dossiers stay, carrying its own progress so an interrupted run resumes instead of restarting; and `erasureCertificate`, which names the refusals as prominently as the erasures and names separately anything already published that still carries the person. The certificate declares create and read for privacy officers and policy admins and NO update or delete: a certificate that can be amended afterwards records what somebody wanted it to say. Both carry an authorization cascade and a retention; the erasure is declared as its own x-openregister-processing activity. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.12.0: three-service-written-schemas-restrict-create. `signingAuditEntry.create` is restricted to docudesk-signing-admins: nothing writes that schema any more (the entries migrated to OpenRegister audit and its config keys are deprecated), so restricting it breaks no path while removing a forgeable signing-history shape. `anonymizationLink` and `documentVersion` were examined and LEFT OPEN, with the reason recorded on each: both are written from #[NoAdminRequired] endpoints by ordinary users and neither write passes `_rbac: false`, so restricting create would fail the anonymise and the finalisation for every user outside the group, which is what restricting prohibitionOverrideAudit.create did in v7.7.0. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.11.0: redaction-and-what-leaves-the-building. Adds `redactionReviewMark`, the record that a person looked at THIS detection run and agreed the redacted copy may be written, and `downloadAgreement`, the terms a download is gated on with who accepted them and when. The mark binds to a detection run rather than to a document: re-running detection leaves the old mark covering findings nobody has looked at, so the gate compares the run and refuses. It records `detectorVersion` so that after a fleet-wide model upgrade it is possible to ASK which approved documents were checked under the old model; an upgrade does not invalidate existing marks, because doing so silently would refuse thousands of already-approved documents in one night. Both schemas declare an authorization cascade: an omitted cascade is OPEN in OpenRegister, and on a review mark that would let any authenticated user sign the approval for their own document. Creating a mark is restricted to docudesk-woo-officers and docudesk-policy-admins. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.10.0: scan-intake-with-separator-sheets. Adds `scanBatch`, one PDF as a scanner delivered it, with an `x-openregister-lifecycle` whose terminal states are `split` and `failed`. A batch that cannot be read fails rather than arriving as one document nobody notices. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.9.0: merge-documents-to-pdf. Adds `mergeJob`, one request to turn several documents into one ordered PDF, with an `x-openregister-lifecycle` on `status` whose terminal states are `done` and `failed`. A failed merge leaves no partial file. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.8.0: documents-from-a-template. Three schemas are added: `pageLayout`, versioned so a layout edited in April cannot rewrite a besluit sent in March; `periodicDocument`, a template rendered over a saved view on a cadence; and `archiveJob`, one bundle of every file on an object with a manifest of what went in and what was left out. `generatedDocument` moves to 1.1.0 and records the layout version it used, the view it rendered over and the review date it falls due on. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.7.0: case-documents-and-the-flat-list. `documentVersion` moves to 1.1.0 and carries `domains[]` and `createdByUser`, so one document serves several domains instead of being copied per domain, and a record whose last domain link is removed stays with its creator. A new `uploadPolicy` schema says what may be uploaded, and one standard policy is seeded. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.6.0: inbound-documents-and-the-worklist. `intakeDocument` moves to 1.1.0 and grows `arrivedWith` (an attachment names the message it came with), `stampedDefaults` and `defaultRule` (what was stamped at creation and which rule chose it), `partySuggestion` (read out of the text, never written as a party), `routing` and `acceptance`, a reading progress, and a `detached` state with the reason and the person who detached it, so a document taken off a record lands on a worklist instead of nowhere. Three schemas are added: `intakeDefaultRule`, `intakeRoutingRule` and `intakePartyCorrection`, the corpus every next party suggestion is ranked against. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.5.0: adds `intakeDocument` for document-intake-inbox, one object per document that arrived before anyone knew which record it belongs to, with an `x-openregister-lifecycle` on `status` whose initial state is `received` and whose terminal states are `assigned` and `rejected`; two waiting examples are seeded so the inbox is not empty on a fresh install. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.4.0: marks the `template` schema shareable (`configuration.x-openregister-shareable`), so OpenRegister's federated configuration sharing offers document templates as a shareable type with no Filinq code; `template` moves 1.1.0 to 1.2.0 so the change reaches existing installs. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.3.0: adds `documentVersion` and `documentFinalityRule` for final-documents-frozen. `documentVersion` is the finalisation record of one document version, carrying an `x-openregister-lifecycle` with a terminal `final` state; it stores no file bytes and no version history, so document-versions keeps Nextcloud files_versions as the only version store. `documentFinalityRule` records which states of a consuming app's record type make its documents final. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.1.0: retires the `product` schema. Pipelinq owns `product` for the fleet, and nothing in Filinq read this copy. It was one of three apps claiming the slug (decidiq, filinq, pipelinq), and on a shared instance a bare relation resolves by slug alone. Removing it from this descriptor is only half the job: the import unions schema ids, so the live row is removed with `occ openregister:schemas:prune-retired --app filinq --slug product --apply`. PREVIOUSLY: Filinq register v8.0.0 — ALL REGISTERS INTO ONE. The five registers this file used to declare (`consent`, `signing`, `templates`, `document`, `dossier`) are replaced by a single register `filinq` carrying all 23 schemas, matching `x-openregister.app`. A SIXTH source was added after the first pass: `docudesk`, the register named for this app's OLD APP ID, which holds 200 objects of this app's own data. It was initially left out as "not one of the five" — true, and beside the point: leaving it standing meant "five into one" quietly shipped an app that owned two registers. It is migrated LAST, so a partial failure that stops before it still leaves the coherent five together. THIS IS NOT A RENAME AND IT DOES NOT MIGRATE ITSELF: an object is bound to its register by NUMERIC id and lives in a per-pair shard table `<prefix>openregister_table_<registerId>_<schemaId>`, so the existing objects sit in tables the new register does not own. The repair step `OCA\Filinq\Repair\ConsolidateRegisters` physically moves them (insert into the target shard table, count the uuids back out, only then delete the source rows), refuses rather than overwrites on a uuid collision, and skips any pair whose target table the import has not created yet. The MAJOR bump is deliberate — the version gate in SettingsInitializer is strictly-greater, so without it nothing reaches an existing install. PREVIOUSLY, v7.11.0 — template-authoring-for-agents (rate card): adds the `product` schema to the `templates` register, exposing `filinq.product.search` + `.get` as DERIVED read tools via `configuration.x-openregister-mcp`. No PHP: the quotation flow composes from tools that already exist (`template.get` for the body, `client`/`lead` from pipelinq, `editDocument` to write into the file the user has open), so the only thing missing was priced data. ⚠️ THE POINT: measured 2026-08-17 across all 160 distinct tools on this instance, NOTHING resolved a product or a rate. Asked to quote "5 hours of dev work" a model has three options — ask, refuse, or invent — and an hourly rate is exactly the plausible-sounding fact it supplies unprompted. On a quotation that is the failure that costs money. The `search` description therefore instructs the agent to return ALL candidates and to ASK when there is no match, never to estimate: "dev work" matches several roles at different rates and picking one silently is how a quote goes out at the wrong price. Writes stay with `docudesk-template-editors` — a rate card is a commercial artefact, consistent with v7.8.0's decision that no Filinq schema exposes a derived create/update/delete verb. ALSO IN v7.11.0 — batch-state-persistence: adds the `anonymizationBatch` schema to the `document` register. Batch anonymisation state used to live ONLY in Nextcloud's distributed cache. `ICacheFactory::createDistributed()` degrades to the local cache class, and that defaults to `OC\Memcache\NullCache` whenever `memcache.local` is unset — which is every Nextcloud that has not been explicitly pointed at APCu/Redis/Memcached, including a stock `occ maintenance:install`. NullCache discards every write and returns null for every read, so the batch record vanished the instant the creating request ended: `POST /api/anonymization/batch/folder` answered 200 with a batchId and fileCount 2, and the very next call `POST /api/anonymization/batch/{id}/extract` answered 404 `Batch not found or expired` (CI run 31963162253). That is the entire multi-file anonymisation flow, broken on every install without a distributed cache. Per ADR-022/ADR-083 the record is now persisted through OpenRegister's object abstraction (BatchStateRepository), with the cache demoted to a read fast path, so the flow is correct with no cache configured at all. `hardValidation:false` because the per-document progress entries evolve with the extraction pipeline and a validation refusal here would re-break the very flow this schema exists to keep working; the batch is app-private transient state, not a record anyone else reads. No `x-openregister-archival` annotation: batches are working state and MUST stay deletable, and an archival annotation makes user-driven deletes throw ArchivalImmutableException. The `authorization` cascade follows v7.9.0's shape rather than being omitted — an omitted cascade is OPEN in OpenRegister, so shipping this schema without one would have re-opened exactly the hole v7.9.0 closed, on a record that lists a user's private filenames. Filinq's own reads and writes go through `_rbac: false` (ownership is enforced in BatchStateService::getBatch), so the cascade governs only direct OpenRegister API access. ⚠️ THE VERSION BUMP IS THE POINT — SettingsInitializer gates the import on `info.version` against the stored `configuration_version`, so a new schema shipped WITHOUT a bump never reaches an existing install and every batch there keeps 404-ing. Previous v7.9.0 — consumer-schema-authorization-audit: declares an `authorization` cascade on ALL 21 schemas. Before this, 20 of 21 declared none, and OpenRegister treats an unconfigured cascade as OPEN — `PermissionHandler::resolveAuthorization()` returns null and every caller is admitted. The Filinq registers carry no register-level cascade either (measured live: all three rows NULL), so nothing filled the gap. MEASURED ON THE DEV INSTANCE BEFORE THE CHANGE, with two ordinary users in no groups and the same organisation: ddauth-bob read ddauth-alice's private template (HTTP 200, full `content`), OVERWROTE its content via PUT (HTTP 200), and duplicated it. This is a WRITE exposure, not only disclosure. The bound is authenticated users within one organisation — multitenancy is a separate axis and stays enforced; it is not anonymous and not cross-tenant. Shape of the fix: `update`/`delete` are restricted on EVERY schema, because that is where the proven harm was; OpenRegister's unconditional owner bypass means a creator keeps full control of their own objects, so this closes cross-user writes without an outage. `read` is additionally restricted only where the data justifies it — financialExtraction + glAccountBooking (supplier IBAN/KvK/BTW), publicationConsent + prohibitionOverrideAudit (GDPR records about identified people), and the four signing schemas (the signer portal resolves signerRecord with `_rbac: false` behind its own token binding in PortalSigningReceiverController, so restricting the cascade does NOT break the signer flow). Everything else keeps `read: authenticated` as a recorded decision, not an omission — reference data (base, customDictionary, glAccountMappingRule) and shared assets (template, huisstijl) must be readable to be applied. ⚠️ `prohibitionOverrideAudit.create` is deliberately `authenticated`, NOT policy-admins: v7.7.0 below records that restricting it re-breaks the fail-closed override path for the ordinary operator who performs the anonymise, raising 500 on every acknowledged override. Four groups are named — docudesk-template-editors, docudesk-policy-admins (already existed), docudesk-financial-admins, docudesk-signing-admins — and OpenRegister provisions declared groups create-only on import, ahead of the content-hash skip. They ship EMPTY on purpose: an empty group denies everyone except admins and object owners, which is the correct default and is immediately visible, rather than back-filling grants nobody chose. Previous v7.8.0 — filinq-mcp-adoption + document-editing-tools: declares `configuration.x-openregister-mcp` on 8 of 21 schemas (template, huisstijl, correspondence, generatedDocument, batchCorrespondenceJob, signingRequest, dossier, base) with `search` + `get` ONLY, `scope: read`, `readOnlyHint: true`. No Filinq schema exposes a derived create/update/delete verb: templates and huisstijl are governance artefacts, correspondence/generatedDocument/batch rows are audit records, and signingRequest is the legal spine of a signature process. The remaining 13 schemas stay off entirely (signature material, citizen contact data, re-identification links, extracted invoice content). Every declared `search.filters` entry was cross-checked against that schema's own `properties` map — an unknown filter fails the whole register import. `generatedDocument.format` additionally gains `docx`, which an agent document edit produces and which the enum predated. ⚠️ THE VERSION BUMP IS THE POINT: SettingsInitializer gates the import on `info.version` against the stored `configuration_version` app-config value, so a dialect change shipped WITHOUT a bump is inert on every existing install — the schemas keep their old configuration and not one derived tool appears, with no error anywhere. Measured on the dev instance before the bump: the four curated #[McpTool] tools were live while all 16 derived tools were absent. Previous v7.7.0 — prohibition-override-audit-schema: adds the `prohibitionOverrideAudit` schema to the `consent` register. `ProhibitionOverrideCommitter::writeAudit()` has always written to `register: consent, schema: prohibitionOverrideAudit`, and that schema was declared NOWHERE — `GET /apps/openregister/api/objects/consent/prohibitionOverrideAudit` answered 404 `Schema not found` while its sibling `publicationProhibition` answered 200 on the same freshly-seeded instance. The write is explicitly fail-closed ('If the audit write fails we MUST NOT proceed to the OR PATCH'), so every acknowledged override raised RuntimeException 500 and NO override could ever be committed. openspec/specs/anonymisation-prohibition-gate/spec.md mandates the schema by name: 'Implementations MUST use a `prohibitionOverrideAudit` schema in `filinq_register.json` for this entry'. Properties are exactly the six the committer writes {ruleId, entityRelationId, fileId, reason, acknowledgedBy, acknowledgedAt}; retention P10Y because an override audit must outlive the P10Y prohibition it released. `authorization: null` matches publicationConsent/anonymizationLink — restricting `create` to policy admins would re-break the same fail-closed path for the ordinary operator who performs the anonymise. See ConductionNL/filinq#428. Previous v7.6.4 — standing-consent-documentid-not-required: `publicationConsent` listed `documentId` in the schema-level `required` array, so OpenRegister created the backing column NOT NULL. Every scope=entity (standing consent) record is document-less by definition, so all 12 seeded standing consents failed to insert with 'null value in column "document_id" violates not-null constraint', and the same constraint blocks PolicyController::createStandingConsent at runtime — the entire "Publish always" surface. The condition is PER RECORD, not per schema, and openspec/specs/consent-management/spec.md already states it: 'documentId MUST be required only for scope=document records'. It is enforced where it can be — ConsentScopeValidator::assertValid(), which rejects a scope=document record without a documentId AND a scope=entity record WITH one. Removing it from the schema's `required` array restores what the spec mandates; nothing is left unvalidated. Previous v7.6.3 — archival-retention-object-shape: fixes six schemas that OpenRegister REJECTED on import, so they never existed on any fresh install. Five (correspondence, signingRequest, signerRecord, signingAuditEntry, batchCorrespondenceJob) declared `x-openregister-archival.retention` as a bare ISO-8601 STRING; OpenRegister's ArchivalAnnotationValidator requires an object `{ default: <duration>, rules?: [] }` and threw 'retention is required and must be an object'. The sixth (publicationProhibition) declared an authorization action `write`, which is not in OpenRegister's CRUD vocabulary (create, read, update, delete) — expanded to create/update/delete, preserving the intent that docudesk-policy-admins may write. ImportHandler catches a per-schema exception, logs it and continues, so the import still answered HTTP 200 'Import successful' while writing only 14 of 20 schemas — which left signing entirely non-functional (signingRequest/signerRecord/signingAuditEntry absent). anonymizationLink and financialExtraction already used the object form; this aligns the rest. No property, slug or retention DURATION changed. Previous v7.6.2 — schema-level-titles-en: re-authored the remaining Dutch schema-level `title` values to English — base 'Grondslag' -> 'Legal Basis', huisstijl 'Huisstijl Configuration' -> 'Branding Configuration' (schema slugs, property keys/titles, enums, descriptions unchanged). Dutch labels now live in l10n/nl.json for the display layer. See openspec/changes (fleet-wide schema-i18n titles rule). Previous v7.6.1 — schema-titles-en: re-authored all Dutch schema property `title` values to English (property names/keys unchanged); Dutch labels now live in l10n/nl.json for the display layer. See openspec/changes (fleet-wide schema-i18n titles rule). Previous v7.6.0 — document-output-destinations-and-bulk-retention: generatedDocument gains additive, nullable fileId/filePath properties, populated when a generation is stored to Files via the new DocumentStorageService (options.output.mode 'files'/'both' on generate, or the now-persisted async bulk job). hardValidation:false, so existing rows remain valid unchanged. See openspec/changes/document-output-destinations-and-bulk-retention/. Previous v7.5.0 — unified-search-provider: corrects the searchable opt-in so only navigable schemas (template, signingRequest) stay searchable and every other schema is searchable:false, keeping Filinq's contribution to OpenRegister's shared Unified Search provider free of dead/unnavigable results. Deep-link routing for template + signingRequest lives in src/manifest.json deepLinks[]. No bespoke OCP\Search\IProvider — org scoping inherited from openregister_objects. See openspec/changes/unified-search-provider/. Previous v7.4.0 — adds customDictionary + customDictionaryTerm to the document register per custom-dictionary-recognition: organisation-scoped, register-i18n-tagged term lists (label, description, colour, matchMode exact/caseInsensitive/wordBoundary, deferred fuzzy flag, active, calculated termCount) matched by CustomDictionaryMatchService and written into OpenRegister's shared entity catalogue as CUSTOM_DICTIONARY occurrences alongside Presidio/regex detections. Seeds one demo dictionary ("Projectnamen") with two demo terms. See openspec/changes/custom-dictionary-recognition/. Previous v7.3.0 — MERGE of Robert's anonimiseren-bij-de-bron work onto development: Woo Art. 5 grondslagen legenda A–S seed (base schema), standing-consent generic-term seeds (publicationConsent, entityType OTHER, notificationStatus skipped), entityType OTHER enum on publicationConsent/publicationProhibition, and EML→PDF assembly. Development schemas + dialect/RBAC fixes are preserved. Previous v5.10.0 — adds glAccountBooking (opaque per-tenant GL-account booking history, keyed by supplierIdentity, fed by the financial-extraction corrections endpoint) and glAccountMappingRule (admin-editable cold-start keyword/category → account rules, no seeded rows — Filinq ships no chart of accounts) to the document register, per ai-gl-account-suggestion. Both hardValidation:true. See openspec/changes/ai-gl-account-suggestion/. Previous v5.9.0 adds the financialExtraction schema to the document register: structured financial field-extraction results (supplier/IBAN/KvK/BTW, invoice number, dates, currency, totals + VAT breakdown, line items) with per-field confidence and an additive corrections[] tuning corpus, per financial-document-field-extraction. hardValidation:true; x-openregister-archival category shipped as an explicit placeholder pending selectielijst-manager sign-off (same pattern as anonymizationLink). See openspec/changes/financial-document-field-extraction/. documentRegistration.title: Document Registration
documentRegistration.description: One entry in the post register: a document that entered or left the building, the unit that registered it, and the number it was given. The number comes from a platform sequence, never from a counter in filinq, so two registrations made at the same moment cannot receive the same one.

direction.description: Whether the document came in or went out. There is no third value: a document that never left is not registered here at all.
direction.title: Direction

registeredAt.description: When the registration was made. This is the moment of registering, not the date printed on the document, and the two differ often enough that conflating them loses the post register's whole point.
registeredAt.title: Registered At

unit.description: The unit that registered it. The number series runs per unit, so this is what decides which sequence the number is drawn from.
unit.title: Unit

registrationNumber.description: The number this registration was given, drawn from a platform sequence and reset each year. Filinq keeps no counter: two registrations made in the same second would otherwise race for one number and one would silently reuse it. NOTE: the series is instance-wide, not per unit. OpenRegister builds the sequence scope as the literal sequence name plus the period, with no placeholder substitution, so a name like filinq-post-{unit} would create one shared series literally called that rather than one per unit. Per-unit series need platform support that does not exist yet.
registrationNumber.title: Registration Number

answers.description: For an outbound registration, the inbound one it answers. The discharge is READ FROM THIS LINK and is never written as a status on the inbound entry, so an inbound entry cannot be marked answered by anything except an actual answer existing.

withdrawnReason.description: Why a number that was allocated was never used. An unexplained gap in a numbered series reads as a lost document; a gap with a reason reads as a decision, and the series stays legible end to end.

withdrawnAt.description: When the allocation was withdrawn. The reason says why and this says when, and a withdrawal with only one of the two is half a record: an auditor reading the series a year later needs to place the gap in time as well as explain it.
withdrawnAt.title: Withdrawn At

anonymizationBatch.description: State of one multi-file anonymisation run: which documents it covers, how far each of them got, and which phase the batch as a whole is in. It was previously held only in Nextcloud's distributed cache, which degrades to a NullCache on any instance without `memcache.local` configured — the record was discarded on write and every follow-up call on the batch answered 404. Written and read exclusively by BatchStateRepository, keyed by the batch UUID (the object UUID is the batchId). Ownership is enforced in BatchStateService::getBatch(), which refuses a batch belonging to another non-admin user.

anonymizationLink.title: Anonymisation Link
anonymizationLink.description: create is `authenticated` DELIBERATELY. The link is written by AnonymizationPersistenceService during an anonymise, which ordinary operators perform through #[NoAdminRequired] endpoints, and that write does not pass `_rbac: false`, so the acting user is the operator. Restricting create to a group would fail the write for every operator outside it, which is exactly what restricting prohibitionOverrideAudit.create did in v7.7.0: 500 on every use of a fail-closed path. Closing the forgery route means making the write system-asserted first; that is a service change with the #283 caveat, not a cascade edit. Koppeling tussen een bronbestand (niet-geanonimiseerd) en zijn geanonimiseerde tegenhanger. Eén record per bronbestand (idempotent op sourceFileId); her-anonimisering werkt hetzelfde record bij. Zowel sourceFileId als anonymizedFileId zijn facetable zodat de OpenRegister zoek-API de koppeling in beide richtingen oplost.

documentVersion.title: Document version
documentVersion.description: create is `authenticated` DELIBERATELY, for the same reason as anonymizationLink: FinalDocumentRepository::save() is reached from #[NoAdminRequired] endpoints when an ordinary user finalises a document, and it does not pass `_rbac: false`. Restricting create would break finalisation for everyone outside the group. The finalisation record of one version of a document. A version is draft or final. Final records who made it final, when, why, and the checksum of the file at that moment. This schema holds no file content and no version history: the bytes stay in Nextcloud files_versions, which document-versions keeps as the only version store.

rejectedBy.title: Rejected by

arrivedWith.description: The intake document of the message this file arrived as an attachment of. Empty on the message itself.
arrivedWith.title: Arrived with

stampedDefaults.description: The metadata a default rule stamped on this document at creation, before any classifier ran.
stampedDefaults.title: Stamped defaults

defaultRule.description: The intake default rule that stamped this document, so a stamped value can always be traced to the rule that chose it. Empty when no rule matched.
defaultRule.title: Default rule

partySuggestion.description: Parties read out of the document text, each with its confidence and the span it came from. A suggestion is never a party record: somebody accepts it first.
partySuggestion.title: Party suggestions

routing.description: The group this document was routed to on arrival, taken from the record type the consuming app declared it against.
routing.title: Routing

acceptance.description: Whether the routed group still has to accept this document, and who accepted it.
acceptance.title: Acceptance

classificationProgress.description: How far the background reading of this document has come, from 0 to 100. A document still being read is listed in the inbox with its progress rather than hidden.
classificationProgress.title: Reading progress

detachReason.description: Why the document was taken off the record it was filed on.
detachReason.title: Detach reason

detachedBy.description: User id of the person who took the document off the record.
detachedBy.title: Detached by

detachedAt.description: When the document was taken off the record (ISO 8601).
detachedAt.title: Detached at

attachmentNotes.description: What happened to the attachments that arrived with this message: each one that was assigned elsewhere is noted here, so the message record never loses sight of a file that came with it.
attachmentNotes.title: Attachment notes

readingState.description: Hoe ver het inlezen is. `failed` is een eigen toestand: een mislukte leesbeurt die `reading` blijft heten is op het scherm niet te onderscheiden van een trage OCR.
readingState.title: Reading State

readingError.description: Waarom het inlezen mislukte. Degene die dit leest is een registrator, niet de ontwikkelaar die de job schreef.
readingError.title: Reading Error

readingUpdatedAt.description: Wanneer de leestoestand voor het laatst veranderde.
readingUpdatedAt.title: Reading Updated At

contentText.description: De tekst die OCR bij binnenkomst uit het bestand las. Dezelfde toegang als het document zelf; de zoekfunctie van de inbox en de classificatie lezen dit veld.
contentText.title: Content Text

documentType.title: Document type
documentType.description: The document type a person confirmed for this document. Set only by a confirmed classification, never by the classifier itself.

correspondent.title: Correspondent
correspondent.description: Who the document is from, as a person confirmed it.

name.title: Name
name.description: The name as the document gives it.

source.title: Source
source.description: Where the name came from: ner (the entities OpenRegister detected) or person (typed by the reviewer).

assign.label: Toewijzen
assign.description: Het document hoort bij dit record. Wie het toewees en wanneer wordt vastgelegd; het bestand verhuist naar de map van het record.

reject.label: Afwijzen
reject.description: Het document hoort hier niet thuis. De reden is verplicht en blijft bij het document staan.

detach.label: Losmaken
detach.description: Het document hoort niet bij dit record. Het komt terug op de werklijst met de reden en de naam van wie het losmaakte.

reassign.label: Opnieuw toewijzen
reassign.description: Het losgemaakte document krijgt alsnog het juiste record.

x-openregister-processing.doelbinding: Read the name and address block out of an arriving document so a clerk can be offered a party to link it to. The suggestion is offered, never filed: no party record is written without a person accepting it.
x-openregister-processing.retentionReference: intakeDocument/x-openregister-archival (P1Y after the document leaves the inbox; suggestions are working data, not the record)

intakeDocument.x-notes: searchable:false on purpose. Unified Search deep-links a result to a DETAIL page, and a waiting intake document has none: the Intake page is a list, and a result that landed nowhere would be worse than no result. What a scanned letter SAYS is searchable through the file itself, which is where the recognised text is written.

subject.nl: Documenten in de postbus konden niet worden gelezen
subject.en: Documents in the inbox could not be read

message.nl: Een of meer documenten konden niet worden ingelezen. Ze staan nog in de postbus en kunnen met de hand worden toegewezen; alleen de tekstherkenning is mislukt.
message.en: One or more documents could not be read. They are still in the inbox and can be assigned by hand; only the text recognition failed.

intakeDefaultRule.title: Intake default rule
intakeDefaultRule.description: Says what metadata an arriving document is stamped with before any classifier looks at it, matched on the channel it came through or on its sender. Nothing arrives unclassified, and every stamped value names the rule that chose it.

name.description: What this rule is called in the list of rules.
name.title: Name

channel.description: The channel this rule matches on. Empty matches every channel.
channel.title: Channel

senderPattern.description: A pattern the sender must contain for this rule to match, such as a domain. Empty matches every sender.
senderPattern.title: Sender pattern

stamps.description: The metadata this rule writes onto an arriving document, such as a document type and a confidentiality.
stamps.title: Stamps

order.description: Which rule wins when several match: the lowest order is applied.
order.title: Order

active.description: An inactive rule stamps nothing, and stays readable so a stamped document can still name the rule that stamped it.
active.title: Active

intakeRoutingRule.title: Intake routing rule
intakeRoutingRule.description: What a consuming app declared about inbound documents on one of its record types: who they go to, and whether somebody has to accept them. Filinq stores and applies the declaration; the record type vocabulary stays the consumer's.

declaringApp.description: App id of the consuming app that made the declaration, such as dossiq. Filinq does not define the record type vocabulary.
declaringApp.title: Declaring app

typeReference.description: The record type this declaration is about, in the consuming app's own vocabulary.
typeReference.title: Type reference

routeTo.description: The group an inbound document on this record type goes to. Empty means no routing.
routeTo.title: Route to

requiresAcceptance.description: Whether the routed group has to accept the document before it counts as filed.
requiresAcceptance.title: Requires acceptance

intakePartyCorrection.title: Intake party correction
intakePartyCorrection.description: One clerk decision about one party suggestion: accepted, edited or rejected. This is the tuning corpus the next suggestion is ranked against, which is why a rejection is stored as carefully as an acceptance.

sender.description: The sender the suggestion was made for. Corrections are ranked against the sender, so the next document from the same party is suggested better.
sender.title: Sender

intakeDocument.description: The intake document the suggestion was shown on.
intakeDocument.title: Intake document

decision.description: What the clerk did with it: accepted as proposed, edited before accepting, or rejected.
decision.title: Decision

accepted.description: What was actually filed, when the clerk accepted or edited. Empty on a rejection.
accepted.title: Accepted

decidedBy.description: User id of the person who decided.
decidedBy.title: Decided by

uploadPolicy.title: Upload policy
uploadPolicy.description: What may be uploaded: which extensions, which media types, how large, and whether a file whose type cannot be read is refused. It is administered rather than written in code, and enforced server-side on every write path, because a policy enforced on one of four paths is not a policy.

allowedExtensions.description: The file extensions an upload may carry. Empty allows every extension.
allowedExtensions.title: Allowed extensions

allowedMediaTypes.description: The media types an upload may be, read from the bytes rather than from the name. Empty allows every type the extensions allow.
allowedMediaTypes.title: Allowed media types

maxSizeBytes.description: The largest upload in bytes. A file over it is refused before the bytes are stored. Zero means no limit.
maxSizeBytes.title: Maximum size

refuseUnknownType.description: Whether a file whose type cannot be read from its bytes is refused, or accepted with a warning.
refuseUnknownType.title: Refuse unknown types

active.description: Only one policy is enforced at a time. An inactive policy stays readable so a refusal can name the policy that refused.
active.title: Active

pageLayout.title: Page layout
pageLayout.description: The paper a generated document leaves the building on: size, margins, header, footer, logo and whether the first page differs. It is versioned, because a layout edited in April must not rewrite a besluit sent in March.

name.description: What this layout is called, such as "Gemeente, besluit".
name.title: Name

layoutVersion.description: The version of this layout. Editing a layout makes a new version rather than changing this one, so a document generated in March still renders the way it did in March.
layoutVersion.title: Layout version

supersedes.description: The layout version this one replaced. The earlier version stays readable, because documents and templates still name it.
supersedes.title: Supersedes

paperSize.description: The paper this layout prints on.
paperSize.title: Paper size

margins.description: The margins in millimetres, as top, right, bottom and left.
margins.title: Margins

header.description: What stands at the top of every page.
header.title: Header

footer.description: What stands at the bottom of every page.
footer.title: Footer

logo.description: File id of the logo this layout prints.
logo.title: Logo

firstPageDiffers.description: Whether the first page carries its own header and footer, as briefpapier usually does.
firstPageDiffers.title: First page differs

firstPageHeader.description: What stands at the top of the first page when it differs.
firstPageHeader.title: First page header

firstPageFooter.description: What stands at the bottom of the first page when it differs.
firstPageFooter.title: First page footer

active.description: Whether this is the version a template resolving by name gets. An inactive version stays readable for the documents that name it.
active.title: Active

periodicDocument.title: Periodic document
periodicDocument.description: A template rendered over the records a saved view returns, on a cadence. Each run writes a new document and leaves every earlier one alone, because last week's besluitenlijst is a record of last week.

name.description: What this periodic document is called, such as "Besluitenlijst".
name.title: Name

viewSlug.description: The saved view whose records the template renders over. A run against a view that no longer exists fails naming it, rather than producing an empty document.
viewSlug.title: Saved view

templateId.description: The template that renders each run.
templateId.title: Template

layout.description: The page layout the output uses.
layout.title: Layout

cadence.description: How often this runs. `onDemand` runs only when somebody asks.
cadence.title: Cadence

lastRunRecords.description: How many records the view returned on the last run.
lastRunRecords.title: Records last read

lastRunDocument.description: The generated document the last run produced. Each run writes a new one; none of them edits an earlier one.
lastRunDocument.title: Last document

lastRunError.description: Why the last attempt failed, such as a view that no longer exists. Empty after a good run. A failed run leaves lastRunDocument pointing at the last good document.
lastRunError.title: Last error

lastRunErrorAt.description: When the last attempt failed (ISO 8601). Empty after a good run.
lastRunErrorAt.title: Last error at

archiveJob.title: Archive job
archiveJob.description: One request to bundle every file on an object into one archive. It records the ceiling in force, what went in, what was left out and why, so a bundle handed to a bezwaarcommissie can be checked rather than trusted.

subject.description: The object whose files were bundled, as register, schema and id.
subject.title: Subject

requestedBy.description: User id of the person who asked for the bundle. The bundle holds what THEY may read, which is why it is recorded.
requestedBy.title: Requested by

ceilingBytes.description: The administered ceiling in force for this job, in bytes.
ceilingBytes.title: Ceiling

includedCount.description: How many files went into the archive.
includedCount.title: Files included

excludedCount.description: How many files did not, each with its reason in the manifest.
excludedCount.title: Files left out

totalBytes.description: The size of what went in, in bytes.
totalBytes.title: Total size

manifest.description: Every file included, and every file left out with the reason. It is in the archive too: a bundle whose contents cannot be checked is a bundle nobody can rely on.
manifest.title: Manifest

fileId.description: File id of the archive produced.
fileId.title: Archive file

errorMessage.description: What went wrong, when something did.
errorMessage.title: Error

mergeJob.title: Merge job
mergeJob.description: One request to turn several documents into one ordered PDF. It keeps the inputs in the order the person chose, what they asked for, and what came out, so a bundle can be traced back to the selection that made it.

inputs.description: The documents to merge, in the order they go in. The order is the user's, and it is stored: a merge that reordered its inputs would produce a bundle nobody asked for.
inputs.title: Inputs

options.description: What the merge was asked for: the cover template, whether to add bookmarks, the target folder and the name of the result.
options.title: Options

requestedBy.description: User id of the person who asked. Every input is read as them, which is why it is recorded.
requestedBy.title: Requested by

hostObject.description: The object the merge was started from, as register, schema and id.
hostObject.title: Host object

resultFileId.description: File id of the merged PDF.
resultFileId.title: Result

pageCount.description: How many pages the result has.
pageCount.title: Pages

progress.description: How far a queued merge has come, from 0 to 100.
progress.title: Progress

lastError.description: What went wrong, naming the file and the backends that were tried. A failed merge writes no partial file.
lastError.title: Last error

conformance.description: What the result actually is: `pdfa-3b` when the archival conversion ran, `pdf` when it was not available on this instance. Said out loud rather than assumed, because a plain PDF that everybody believes is PDF/A-3b is the failure this field exists to prevent.
conformance.title: Conformance

fail.label: Mislukken
fail.description: De samenvoeging is gestopt. Er staat geen half bestand: wat er niet helemaal is, is er niet.

printJob.title: Print job
printJob.description: Letters sent to print as one job, and what the print service reported back.

requestedBy.description: User id of the person who sent the letters to print.
requestedBy.title: Requested by

templateId.description: The template the letters were made from.
templateId.title: Template

total.description: How many letters the job holds.
total.title: Letters

rendered.description: How many letters have a PDF.
rendered.title: Ready

errors.description: How many letters could not be made.
errors.title: Errors

files.description: The PDFs in the app data folder, one per letter, in order.
files.title: Files

printConfig.description: Duplex, colour, paper tray and stapling for the printer.
printConfig.title: Print settings

manifest.description: One entry per letter with its file name and whether it was made.
manifest.title: Manifest

statusDetails.description: What the print service said with its last status.
statusDetails.title: Printer message

scanBatch.title: Scan batch
scanBatch.description: One PDF as a scanner delivered it, holding several documents. Filinq cuts it at the separator sheets it printed itself and hands each segment to the intake inbox. The batch records what it was cut into, so a missing document can be traced back to the sheet that should have separated it.

file.description: Nextcloud file id of the batch the scanner delivered: one PDF holding several documents.
file.title: File

scannerId.description: The scan profile the batch came from, which is what says how to cut it.
scannerId.title: Scanner

receivedAt.description: When the batch landed in the watched folder (ISO 8601).
receivedAt.title: Received at

separatorMode.description: How the batch is cut: on the QR separator sheets filinq printed, or on blank pages.
separatorMode.title: Separator mode

pageCount.description: How many pages the batch held.
pageCount.title: Pages

segments.description: The intake documents this batch was cut into, in order, each with the pages it took.
segments.title: Segments

lastError.description: Why the batch could not be cut. A batch that could not be read is failed, not quietly delivered as one document.
lastError.title: Last error

split.label: Splitsen
split.description: De batch is geknipt op de scheidingsvellen. Elk segment staat als los document in de postbak.

fail.label: Mislukken
fail.description: De batch kon niet gelezen worden. Er wordt niets afgeleverd: een batch die als één document binnenkomt terwijl er scheidingsvellen in zaten, valt niemand op.

redactionReviewMark.title: Redaction Review Mark
redactionReviewMark.description: Het bewijs dat een mens de gedetecteerde entiteiten van DIT detectie-uitvoering heeft bekeken en akkoord is dat de geredigeerde kopie geschreven mag worden. Detectie is een oordeel van een machine over waar de namen staan; het besluit dat deze kopie het pand mag verlaten is van een mens. De markering hoort bij een detectie-uitvoering, niet bij het document: wordt de detectie opnieuw gedraaid, dan is de markering van de vorige uitvoering en dekt zij de nieuwe bevindingen niet.

document.description: Het document waarvan de geredigeerde kopie geschreven mag worden.
document.title: Document

detectionRun.description: De detectie-uitvoering die is bekeken. De markering dekt alleen deze uitvoering.
detectionRun.title: Detection Run

checkedBy.description: Wie het heeft gecontroleerd. Een controle die niemand heeft ondertekend is een controle waarover niemand bevraagd kan worden.
checkedBy.title: Checked By

detectorVersion.description: De versie van het detectiemodel dat deze uitvoering heeft geproduceerd. Vastgelegd zodat na een vlootbrede modelupgrade te vinden is welke goedgekeurde documenten onder het oude model zijn gecontroleerd. Een upgrade laat bestaande markeringen staan: ze zijn geldig voor hun eigen uitvoering, en het automatisch ongeldig verklaren zou duizenden reeds goedgekeurde documenten in een nacht weigeren.
detectorVersion.title: Detector Version

entityCount.description: Hoeveel entiteiten deze uitvoering vond, zodat een controle achteraf te plaatsen is.
entityCount.title: Entity Count

downloadAgreement.title: Download Agreement
downloadAgreement.description: De voorwaarden waaronder een geredigeerd document gedownload mag worden, en de vastlegging wie ze wanneer heeft aanvaard. Een nieuwe versie vraagt opnieuw: aanvaarding van een oudere tekst is aanvaarding van iets anders.

version.description: De versie van de tekst. Een nieuwe versie vraagt opnieuw om aanvaarding.
version.title: Version

text.description: De voorwaarden zoals de downloader ze leest.
text.title: Text

acceptedVersion.description: Welke versie is aanvaard. Losgehouden van `version` zodat een aanvaarding van een oudere tekst zichtbaar blijft in plaats van mee te schuiven.
acceptedVersion.title: Accepted Version

subjectErasureRequest.title: Subject Erasure Request
subjectErasureRequest.description: Een verzoek van een betrokkene om uit de documenten te worden verwijderd, terwijl de dossiers zelf blijven bestaan. Anders dan een archivering, die start als een bewaartermijn afloopt, start dit als iemand een recht uitoefent: de betrokkene heeft deze documenten niet gekozen, en er loopt een wettelijke termijn. De voortgang staat op het verzoek zelf, zodat een afgebroken run hervat kan worden in plaats van opnieuw te beginnen.

identifiers.title: Identifiers
identifiers.description: Elke schrijfwijze waaronder deze persoon in documenten voorkomt. Eén naam vindt niet elk voorkomen.

requestedAt.description: Wanneer het verzoek binnenkwam. De termijn loopt hiervandaan.
requestedAt.title: Requested At

progress.title: Progress
progress.description: Welke documenten al gedaan zijn, zodat een afgebroken run verdergaat waar hij stopte en niet opnieuw over alles loopt.

lastDocument.description: Het laatst voltooide document, het hervatpunt.
lastDocument.title: Last Document

excluded.title: Excluded
excluded.description: Voorkomens die een behandelaar vóór de run heeft uitgesloten, met reden. Zonder reden is een uitsluiting niet te verantwoorden.

results.title: Results
results.description: What happened to each document: erased, refused with the obligation, excluded, or failed with the reason.

name.title: Name
name.description: The file name when the run reached it.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the document was not erased.

obligations.title: Obligations
obligations.description: The obligations that refused the document, each with who must decide.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the document was not erased.

newVersionFileId.title: New version file id
newVersionFileId.description: The file id of the version written beside a final document.

mappingEntriesDestroyed.title: Mapping entries destroyed
mappingEntriesDestroyed.description: How many reversible pseudonymisation entries for the person were destroyed.

certificate.title: Certificate
certificate.description: The certificate issued when every document was reached.

x-openregister-archival.reason: Het verzoek is het bewijs dat iemand zijn recht heeft uitgeoefend en wat daarmee is gebeurd; het moet de behandeltermijn en een eventuele klacht overleven.

x-openregister-processing.purpose: Uitvoeren van een verwijderingsverzoek van een betrokkene, terwijl de dossiers blijven bestaan.
x-openregister-processing.legalBasis: AVG artikel 17, met artikel 17 lid 3 als grond voor de weigeringen.

erasureCertificate.title: Erasure Certificate
erasureCertificate.description: Wat er werkelijk is gewist, wat is geweigerd en waarom, en wat elders al gepubliceerd is en dus opnieuw gepubliceerd moet worden. Het certificaat noemt de weigeringen even prominent als de wissingen: een certificaat dat alleen opsomt wat is gewist leest als een afgerond verzoek.

erased.title: Erased
erased.description: Per document het aantal gewiste voorkomens.

refused.title: Refused
refused.description: Per geweigerd document de verplichting en wie erover beslist.

needsRepublishing.title: Needs Republishing
needsRepublishing.description: Reeds gepubliceerde kopieën die de persoon nog bevatten. Het volgende probleem van de verzoeker, dus apart genoemd.

complete.description: Alleen waar als er niets is geweigerd en niets opnieuw gepubliceerd hoeft te worden.
complete.title: Complete

ground.title: Ground
ground.description: The legal ground of the request.

excluded.title: Excluded
excluded.description: Occurrences the operator left in place, with the reason.

occurrence.title: Occurrence
occurrence.description: The document, or the document and the identifier.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Why the document was not erased.

mappingEntriesDestroyed.title: Mapping entries destroyed
mappingEntriesDestroyed.description: How many reversible pseudonymisation entries for the person were destroyed.

documentRecordsDeleted.title: Document records deleted
documentRecordsDeleted.description: Always 0: an erasure removes the person from documents and deletes no document record.

x-openregister-archival.reason: Het certificaat is het enige bewijs dat een wissing is uitgevoerd en wat er is geweigerd; het moet het verzoek zelf overleven.

publicationRecord.title: Publication
publicationRecord.description: One document, or one dossier as a bundle, on its way to the publication platform: whether it may be published, the Woo metadata, and what happened to it there.

subjectType.description: What is published: one document or a dossier as a bundle.
subjectType.title: Subject

documentFileRef.description: The Nextcloud file id of the original document. The original is never handed off.
documentFileRef.title: Document

dossierRef.description: The dossier the document belongs to, if any.
dossierRef.title: Dossier

redactedFileRef.description: The Nextcloud file id of the redacted copy that is published.
redactedFileRef.title: Redacted copy

entitiesReviewed.description: Whether a person checked the detected entities of the redacted copy.
entitiesReviewed.title: Entities reviewed

consentClear.description: Whether every consent request for the document allows publication.
consentClear.title: Consent clear

prohibitionsClear.description: Whether no active publication prohibition matches the document.
prohibitionsClear.title: Prohibitions clear

readinessEvaluatedAt.description: When the three checks last ran. Readiness is never trusted beyond that moment.
readinessEvaluatedAt.title: Readiness checked at

readinessReasons.description: What still blocks publication, one line per reason. Names record ids, never personal data.
readinessReasons.title: Why not ready

wooCategory.description: The Woo information category as OpenCatalogi's code, for example infocat009. A record stored before register 8.46.0 may hold the TOOI code (c_8c840238); the hand-off translates it.
wooCategory.title: Information category

documentsoort.description: The kind of document, for example besluit.
documentsoort.title: Document type

publisher.description: The publishing organisation as a TOOI identifier.
publisher.title: Publisher

endpointPublicationRef.description: The id of the publication object at the publication platform.
endpointPublicationRef.title: Publication at the platform

handoffAt.description: When the publication was handed to the platform.
handoffAt.title: Handed off at

depublicationRequestedAt.description: When the withdrawal was asked for.
depublicationRequestedAt.title: Withdrawal requested at

destructionDate.description: The date the source system destroys the document; passed to the platform so the publication goes offline then too.
destructionDate.title: Destruction date

destructionDateSource.description: Where the destruction date came from, for example a selection list.
destructionDateSource.title: Destruction date from

accessibilityState.description: Whether the redacted copy kept its tag structure, as the redaction recorded it: preserved, degraded, not-applicable or unknown. Degraded and unknown warn, or block the hand-off when the accessibility gate is set to block.
accessibilityState.title: Accessibility

accessibilityOverrideReason.description: Why this document may be published although its redacted copy lost its accessibility, when the accessibility gate blocks. Recorded with the hand-off.
accessibilityOverrideReason.title: Accessibility override reason

publicationLogEntry.title: Publication log entry
publicationLogEntry.description: One step in the life of a publication, written once and never changed.

publicationRecordRef.description: The publication this step belongs to.
publicationRecordRef.title: Publication

actor.description: The user id of who did it, or system.
actor.title: By

details.description: What was decided or said, for example the reason for a withdrawal.
details.title: Details

snapshot.description: The readiness and metadata at that moment: verdicts and record ids only, no personal data.
snapshot.title: State then

ocrResult.title: OCR result
ocrResult.description: What the last text recognition run on one file found: how sure it was, the languages and resolution it used, and how much text it recovered. It never holds the text itself; that lives in OpenRegister's chunks like all extracted text.

fileId.description: The Nextcloud file id. One result per file: a new run updates it.
fileId.title: File

languages.description: The language models the run used, such as nld+eng.
languages.title: Languages

dpi.description: The resolution a PDF page was rendered at before recognition.
dpi.title: Resolution (DPI)

textLength.description: How many characters of text the run recovered.
textLength.title: Text length

triggeredBy.description: Whether a person started the run or the anonymisation pipeline did.
triggeredBy.title: Started by

conformanceReport.title: Conformance report
conformanceReport.description: What veraPDF found when it checked one PDF against the PDF/A standard: the level, the verdict, the rules broken and the fonts missing. Rule references and font names only, never text from the document.

fileId.description: The Nextcloud file id. One report per file and subject: a new check updates it.
fileId.title: File

subject.description: Whether the stored file itself was checked, or the PDF/A-3 copy a conversion of it made.
subject.title: What was checked

flavour.description: The PDF/A level checked against, such as 3b: the one the document claims, or 3b when it claims none.
flavour.title: PDF/A level

compliant.description: Whether veraPDF found the document to meet every rule of that level.
compliant.title: Conforms

failedRuleCount.description: How many rules of the level the document breaks.
failedRuleCount.title: Rules failed

failedRules.description: The rules broken, by reference only. Never text from the document.
failedRules.title: Failed rules

ruleId.title: Rule
ruleId.description: The rule, as standard, clause and test number.

specification.title: Standard
specification.description: The standard the rule comes from, such as ISO 19005-3:2012.

testNumber.title: Test
testNumber.description: The test number within the clause.

checksFailed.title: Places
checksFailed.description: How many places in the document break the rule.

fontsNotEmbedded.description: The names of fonts the document uses without carrying them, which an e-depot rejects.
fontsNotEmbedded.title: Fonts not embedded

guidance.description: The advice that fits the failure.

pseudonymMap.title: Pseudonym map

legalHoldCase.title: Legal hold case
legalHoldCase.description: One legal matter (a lawsuit, an audit, a Woo appeal) and the records it freezes. While the case is active, every record in its scope carries an OpenRegister legal hold, so no destruction list picks it up, and its files carry an app lock where files_lock is installed. Releasing the case lifts a hold only when no other active case still covers the record. A released case stays: the hold register is itself a record.

objects.name: F — Betrekkingen met andere staten

objects.name: H — Opsporing en vervolging van strafbare feiten

objects.name: I — Inspectie, controle en toezicht

objects.name: K — Concurrentiegevoelige bedrijfsgegevens
